note: Recorded sample output for demos and tests, written for the clinic-booking sample brief.

output.summary: A short, calm booking flow that suits people in pain: three steps, first available by default, large targets and a call option everywhere. Two issues must be fixed before release: the late-cancellation fee isn't stated before booking, and the cancel sheet makes cancelling the most prominent action.
strengths: Details are asked only after a time is chosen, and kept if that time is taken
'First available' default matches what most new patients want
Every error says what was kept and offers a way forward, including a call
Health data is limited to four intake questions, asked after booking and only for first visits
48pt targets and full-width time rows instead of a grid

findings.title: Late-cancellation fee isn't stated before booking
findings.evidence: Confirm has no policy line at all. The only mention is on the late-change screen, which says 'a late-cancellation fee may apply' with no amount.
findings.detail: People book without knowing a late change costs money, then find out when it's too late to avoid it. That's unfair to patients and generates disputes for reception.
findings.recommendation: Add one plain line above Confirm booking: free to change or cancel up to 24 hours before, then the fee amount. State the amount on the late-change screen and the exact deadline on Booked and in the confirmation.

findings.title: 'Cancel appointment' is styled as the main action in the cancel sheet
findings.evidence: The destructive action is the filled primary button at the top of the sheet, where the thumb lands; 'Keep appointment' is a text button at the bottom.
findings.detail: People with tremor or in pain can cancel by mistake, and losing an appointment can mean waiting days for another. It also looks the same as 'Confirm booking', the flow's positive action.
findings.recommendation: Make 'Keep appointment' the primary action and show 'Cancel appointment' as a destructive (danger, unfilled) button, last and visually separated.

findings.title: Rescheduling reuses the booking wording
findings.evidence: When coming from 'Change date or time', the steps still say 'Check and confirm', 'Confirm booking' and 'You're booked'.
findings.detail: A returning patient may think they've made a second booking rather than moved the first.
findings.recommendation: Add reschedule variants: 'Confirm new time', 'Your appointment has moved', and show the old time crossed out in the summary.

findings.title: Web content column width isn't specified in the UI blocks
findings.evidence: The 640px column is only in notes; the rendered web frame stretches fields across the full 1280px width.
findings.detail: Very wide fields and lines are harder to scan, and the primary button ends up far from the fields.
findings.recommendation: Make the 640px maximum width part of the web layout spec and check it in the built pages.

findings.title: Physio chips push times below the fold on small phones
findings.evidence: Seven physio chips plus five day chips wrap to about five rows before the first time appears on a 375pt-wide screen.
findings.detail: People in pain have to scroll before they see a single time, although most want 'First available'.
findings.recommendation: Show 'First available' and the person's last physio as chips, with 'Choose a physio' opening a select for the rest.

findings.title: No way to see past appointments
findings.detail: Returning patients sometimes want to check when they last came or who they saw.
findings.recommendation: Consider a 'Past appointments' link on Home in a later release.

heuristicsReviewed.note: Step counter, held-time note, and every loading state is announced.

heuristicsReviewed.heuristic: H2 Match between system and the real world
heuristicsReviewed.note: Plain words: 'physio', 'change date or time', clinics named by street.
Back keeps choices; 'Change the time instead' offered when cancelling.
Fee not stated before booking (C1); cancel styled as the main action (C2).
The summary card follows the person through the steps; details are kept after errors.

heuristicsReviewed.heuristic: H7 Flexibility and efficiency of use
heuristicsReviewed.note: 'First available' by default; returning patients can go straight to times.
The physio chips wrap to three rows on small phones (C5).

heuristicsReviewed.heuristic: H9 Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
heuristicsReviewed.note: Errors say what was kept and offer a call; slot-taken keeps the details.
Hints on which type to choose and why details are asked; calling is always offered.

wcagChecked.note: Headings label each choice group; fields have visible labels.
Selected chips and times show a check and the word 'Selected'.
All text pairs meet 4.5:1 in light and dark on every platform.
Cancel sheet moves focus in and back; error summaries take focus.
Focus states are defined for every interactive component.
Field errors are named in text next to the field.
No icon-only controls without names; chips are a radio group.
Loading, booked and cancelled states are announced.
A booking that can incur a fee is confirmed without stating the fee (C1).
The 10-minute hold must not lose the person's details when it lapses; confirm in build.
